findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "check_manufacturability" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Use this after uploading CAD files and before quoting, when the user asks whether a part can be made, wants a DFM (design for manufacturing) review, or asks wha…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_manufacturability · Private data: upload_cad_for_quote, check_manufacturability, get_quotes, preview_order, get_part, build_rfq · Public sink: upload_cad_for_quote, build_rfq · Destructive: upload_cad_for_quote, find_equivalents, get_test_protocol, check_test_result.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_manufacturability · Private data: upload_cad_for_quote, check_manufacturability, get_quotes, preview_order, get_part, build_rfq · Public sink: upload_cad_for_quote, build_rfq · Destructive: upload_cad_for_quote, find_equivalents, get_test_protocol, check_test_result

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
